chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: Discrimination at the Spanish regional centers
summary: Black clubs had no problem, but the Centro Gallego and Centro Asturiano were white Spanish organizations that pressured black musicians.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you went to a club, did you have any racial discrimination, like going through the back door or things like that?

......because those clubs, seventy-five percent, they was black, mulato or whatever you want to call it. The only problem that we had was when we went to the Centro Gallego or to the Centro Asturiano. That was a white, pure white organization from Spain; all those states from Spain like Galicia, Asturias, Vasco, you know from....
And that's when you ah - ah - ......
You start to feel the pressure.
Okay, but there was where you encountered discrimination.
